artifacts.name: About this indicator
artifacts.summary: Counts the street features that decide whether a walk is possible for someone older or less mobile: benches to rest on, public toilets, dropped or tactile kerbs, and crossings that signal audibly. It reports them at the short distances that actually apply — 200 metres between res
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: age_friendly_streets · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.39. 0 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of age-friendly features density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 6 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over age-friendly features density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: age_friendly_streets · reachability: straight-line distance.

Only 6 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over age-friendly features per 1,000 residents: **High-High** = a well-supplied neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a poorly-supplied one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

artifacts.name: Age-friendliness (weakest link)
artifacts.summary: A combined layer (weakest link) of 1×Benches, 1×Public toilets, 1×Crossable kerbs, per sub-area. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Map algebra: for each administrative sub-area, the normalised densities of the input categories are combined by **weakest link** — 1×Benches, 1×Public toilets, 1×Crossable kerbs — into a single value. Each category is first rescaled to 0–1 across sub-areas, so the value is a unitless index. Use it to express a composite index (e.g. a weighted suitability score) as one layer instead of several.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: age_friendly_streets · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Age-friendly features per resident (surface)
artifacts.summary: A continuous surface of age-friendly features per 1,000 residents — provision relative to need, without administrative boundaries. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Kernel-smoothed age-friendly features density divided by population density on the same grid, scaled to per 1,000 residents. Unlike the per-capita choropleth this owes nothing to administrative boundaries, so gradients *within* a district are visible; the trade-off is that it is a smoothed estimate rather than an exact count per area. Cells with fewer than 1 residents are left transparent, because dividing by a nearly empty cell produces a large figure that reflects the arithmetic rather than good provision. Populated cells with no feature within reach are drawn in the lowest class, not left blank — they are the worst-served places and the reason to read this map.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: age_friendly_streets · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest age-friendly feature. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.
